mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has recovered from -25.3% (t-2w) to -8.6% (t-0w), a 16.7-point improvement. This sustained workplace recovery signals resumption of commuting routines and weekday foot traffic, which mechanically lifts retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 16.7 points over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to below -15% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility remains severely depressed at -18.3% (t-0w), indicating persistent avoidance of public transport. This suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility because transit-dependent populations cannot easily reach retail destinations, keeping RETAIL_REC negative over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -18.3% in t-0w, unchanged from t-1w trend
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -10% in week t+1 and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises above the prior 28-day mean within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has collapsed from +10.0% (t-2w) to -4.4% (t-0w), a 14.4-point drop. This signals loss of outdoor leisure activity substitution. When parks decline sharply, consumers redirect discretionary time to indoor retail-and-recreation venues, producing a compensatory increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0% after being positive
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 14.4 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean, or PARKS remains negative and continues to decline in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has remained stable at 9-13% above baseline across all four weeks, indicating consistent essential-goods purchasing. When essential mobility is stable and high, consumers gain confidence to make discretionary retail trips. This confidence effect, combined with workplace recovery, drives RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 5% or WORKPLACES reverses below -15%, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has declined from 15.1% (t-2w) to 11.4% (t-0w), a 3.7-point drop. This signals gradual relaxation of stay-at-home behavior or policy constraints. As residential confinement eases, people venture out more frequently to retail-and-recreation destinations, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 3.7 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 14% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Transit mobility remains severely depressed at -18.3% while workplace mobility has recovered to -8.6%. This mismatch indicates that workers are returning via private transport or remote work, not public transit. Without transit recovery, retail-and-recreation mobility cannot fully recover because transit-dependent populations remain constrained, keeping RETAIL_REC negative over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves more than 10 points while TRANSIT remains below -15%
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -10% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above the prior 28-day mean despite the transit-workplace mismatch.

mechanism_narrative: Retail-and-recreation mobility has been consistently negative (-4.7% to -9.4%) across all four weeks, with no recovery trend visible. This persistent suppression indicates structural constraints (policy, seasonal, or behavioral) that are not reversing. Absent a shock to TRANSIT or WORKPLACES, RETAIL_REC will remain negative over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC remains below -4% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC ranged -4.7% to -9.4% across all four weeks with no upward trend
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above 0% in week t+1 or exceeds the prior 28-day mean by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility remains elevated at 11.4% (t-0w) while retail-and-recreation is deeply negative at -8.7%. This inversion indicates that people are staying home more than baseline but avoiding retail venues specifically. If residential confinement does not decline further and retail-specific avoidance persists, RETAIL_REC will remain negative over the next four weeks despite overall mobility activity.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 10% and RETAIL_REC below -8% simultaneously
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises above -2% despite residential elevation, indicating retail-specific avoidance has ended.
